title: Validating the skellam package
text: definition, \(P(X = x) = \sum_k P(Y_1 = k + x)\,P(Y_2 = k)\). Summing series directly slow exact, makes good reference. probabilities also add one, including rates far beyond series can handle quickly: one rate zero distribution Poisson, Poisson turned upside :
code: pmf_by_sum <- function(x, l1, l2) {   k <- max(0, -x):(abs(x) + 200 + 20 * (l1 + l2))   sum(dpois(k + x, l1) * dpois(k, l2)) } x <- -10:15 for (L in list(c(1.5, 0.5), c(12, 8))) {   ref <- vapply(x, pmf_by_sum, 0, l1 = L[1], l2 = L[2])   cat(sprintf("lambda = (%g, %g): largest relative difference %.1e\n",               L[1], L[2], max(abs(dskellam(x, L[1], L[2]) / ref - 1)))) } #> lambda = (1.5, 0.5): largest relative difference 6.7e-15 #> lambda = (12, 8): largest relative difference 2.7e-15 for (L in list(c(1.5, 0.5), c(12, 8), c(1e4, 1e4), c(1e6, 1e6))) {   s <- sqrt(sum(L)); m <- L[1] - L[2]   x <- seq(floor(m - 30 * s), ceiling(m + 30 * s))   cat(sprintf("lambda = (%g, %g): 1 - sum = %.1e\n", L[1], L[2],               1 - sum(dskellam(x, L[1], L[2])))) } #> lambda = (1.5, 0.5): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 #> lambda = (12, 8): 1 - sum = -8.9e-16 #> lambda = (10000, 10000): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 #> lambda = (1e+06, 1e+06): 1 - sum = 0.0e+00 all.equal(dskellam(0:10, 5, 0), dpois(0:10, 5)) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(dskellam(-(0:10), 0, 5), dpois(0:10, 5)) #> [1] TRUE

title: Validating the skellam package
text: pskellam(x) equal running sum dskellam x, two tails add one. discrete distribution quantile function returns smallest integer \(x\) \(P(X \le x) \ge p\). Feeding value distribution function back must therefore return \(x\), tails log scale:
code: l1 <- 12; l2 <- 8 x <- -40:50 max(abs(pskellam(x, l1, l2) - cumsum(dskellam(x, l1, l2)))) #> [1] 1.110223e-15 max(abs(pskellam(x, l1, l2) + pskellam(x, l1, l2, lower.tail = FALSE) - 1)) #> [1] 0 x <- -15:25 all(qskellam(pskellam(x, l1, l2), l1, l2) == x) #> [1] TRUE all(qskellam(pskellam(x, l1, l2, lower.tail = FALSE), l1, l2, lower.tail = FALSE) == x) #> [1] TRUE all(qskellam(pskellam(x, l1, l2, log.p = TRUE), l1, l2, log.p = TRUE) == x) #> [1] TRUE qskellam(c(0, 0.025, 0.5, 0.975, 1), l1, l2) #> [1] -Inf   -5    4   13  Inf

title: Validating the skellam package
text: rskellam draws difference two Poisson variates. compare observed frequencies 20,000 draws probabilities dskellam, pooling sparse tails every cell expects least 5 observations. Observed frequencies 20,000 draws (bars) expected frequencies dskellam (points).
code: N <- 20000 lambda1 <- 1.5; lambda2 <- 0.5 z <- rskellam(N, lambda1, lambda2) c(mean = mean(z), expected = lambda1 - lambda2) #>     mean expected  #>   1.0044   1.0000 c(variance = var(z), expected = lambda1 + lambda2) #> variance expected  #> 2.013481 2.000000  lo <- qskellam(0.001, lambda1, lambda2); hi <- qskellam(0.999, lambda1, lambda2) cells <- lo:hi prob <- dskellam(cells, lambda1, lambda2) prob[1] <- pskellam(lo, lambda1, lambda2)                                 # all x <= lo prob[length(prob)] <- pskellam(hi - 1, lambda1, lambda2, lower.tail = FALSE)  # all x >= hi obs <- table(factor(pmin(pmax(z, lo), hi), levels = cells)) chisq.test(obs, p = prob) #>  #>  Chi-squared test for given probabilities #>  #> data:  obs #> X-squared = 3.2351, df = 9, p-value = 0.9542 plot(cells, as.vector(obs), type = "h", lwd = 6, col = "grey70",      xlab = "x", ylab = "Frequency", main = "") points(cells, N * prob, pch = 19, col = "#0072B2") legend("topright", c("rskellam", "N * dskellam"), lwd = c(6, NA), pch = c(NA, 19),        col = c("grey70", "#0072B2"), bty = "n")

title: The Skellam Distribution — skellam
text: \(Y_1 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_1)\) \(Y_2 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_2)\) independent, \(X = Y_1 - Y_2\) Skellam distribution probability mass function $$P(X = x) = e^{-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)} (\lambda_1/\lambda_2)^{x/2}   I_{|x|}(2\sqrt{\lambda_1 \lambda_2}), \qquad x = \ldots, -1, 0, 1, \ldots$$ \(I_\nu\) modified Bessel function first kind. mean \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2\) variance \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2\). (\(Y_1\) \(Y_2\) correlated Poisson variables means \(\mu_i\) correlation \(\rho\), difference still Skellam, \(\lambda_i = \mu_i - \rho\sqrt{\mu_1 \mu_2}\).) functions follow conventions stats distribution functions: arguments recycled common length (warning lengths multiples), missing values propagate, invalid rates probabilities give NaN warning, non-integer x density 0 (warning), qskellam returns smallest integer \(x\) \(P(X \le x) \ge p\) (lower.tail = TRUE), qskellam(pskellam(x, ...), ...) recovers x. Numerical methods. dskellam evaluates log Bessel function directly, log = TRUE finite accurate input: besselI reliable, uniform asymptotic expansion large orders, stable downward recurrence large arguments, power series besselI underflows. relative error \(10^{-12}\) rates least \(10^7\), \(10^{-9}\) extremely unequal large rates \((10^6, 10^3)\). pskellam uses non-central chi-square identity Johnson (1959) pchisq \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \le 10^4\), otherwise, well tails pchisq underflows, sums log-pmf directly toward nearer tail, far tails exact log scale. qskellam starts Cornish-Fisher approximation searches integers pskellam. rskellam returns difference two rpois draws. dskellam.sp pskellam.sp second-order saddlepoint approximation pmf Lugannani-Rice approximation cdf Butler's second continuity correction (Butler 2007). relative error order \(1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)^2\) \(1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\) respectively; provided users want approximations used dskellam pskellam.

title: skellam 0.2.5
text: dskellam() now accurate (relative error 1e-12) rates least 1e7, log = TRUE finite deepest tails. Previously, rates 5e4 pmf computed saddlepoint approximation applied half correction term (probabilities summed 1 - 1/(32 lambda)), log = TRUE returned natural-scale probabilities , dskellam(500, 3, 2, log = TRUE) -Inf. new core (R/bessel.R) evaluates log Bessel function uniform asymptotic expansion large orders, stable downward recurrence large arguments, power series besselI() underflows. pskellam() now accurate (relative error 1e-11) rates. lambda1 + lambda2 = 1e4 non-central chi-square route pchisq() slow, lost accuracy, beyond 5e5 stopped converging returned wrong value (pskellam(0, 1e6, 1e6) gave 0.875; answer 0.500). rates, tail pchisq() underflows, now use direct log-space summation pmf, far tails exact log scale never negative. Quantiles large rates correspondingly faster: qskellam() rates 1e6 takes 0.04 s instead 0.7 s warnings. dskellam.sp() now honours log = TRUE applies full second-order saddlepoint correction. skellam.mle() skellam.reg() longer switch warnings rest R session (set options(warn = -1) never restored ). dskellam() returns NA missing x instead stopping “missing value TRUE/FALSE needed”; one NA longer breaks whole vector. dskellam() returns 0 (-Inf log scale) non-integer x, dpois() , instead density trunc(x). Values within 1e-7 integer treated integer. dskellam() warns argument lengths multiples (check never fire), keeps names(x), returns 0 infinite x. pskellam(q, 0, 0) 0 1 instead NaN, zero rate now computed exactly ppois() (previously exact 0 pchisq() sent saddlepoint approximation, divides zero rate). pskellam() returns NA missing q (NaN), 0/1 q = -Inf/Inf (NaN warnings), warns recycling, keeps names(q). qskellam() lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE, longer returns one correct quantile whenever p exactly cdf value. qskellam(pskellam(x, ...), ...) == x now holds tails scales. qskellam(1, ...) returns Inf (-Inf), p = 0/p = 1 give ends support tails log scale (qskellam(0, 3, 2, log.p = TRUE) stopped error). qskellam() lambda1 = 0 longer returns one correct quantile cdf values. qskellam() validates input: p outside [0, 1] negative rates give NaN warning (Inf error), missing values give NA (error). warns recycling keeps names(p). qskellam() longer gives different answers options(verbose = TRUE) set. rskellam() returns integer vector, like rpois(); invalid rates give NA “NAs produced” (NaN). draws unchanged given seed. skellam.mle() longer returns negative rates. samples whose variance exceed absolute mean (including constant samples) returned negative “Poisson rate” (1.5, -1.5); -zero sample stopped “non-finite value supplied ‘nlm’”. now maximizes profile likelihood admissible range optimize() returns boundary estimate maximum: (0, 0) zeros, (c, 0) constant c > 0. Missing, non-integer observations give clear errors. return value keeps components (iters now counts log-likelihood evaluations). skellam.reg() now works rate, gives identical results repeated calls, reports problems. used besselI() without scaling, overflowed rates 360 underflowed starting values data large differences (“function evaluated initial parameters”); started random values (rnorm()) without seed, two calls data differed; chained three optimizers without checking convergence. now uses dskellam(log = TRUE), starts deterministically intercept-moment estimates, runs one BFGS optimization analytic gradient, warns optimizer converge information matrix inverted (standard errors NA). Observations missing values removed warning (previously missing covariate silently misaligned y x).
